Diego M.: Hey team, first-day question. I'm on Windows 11 with WSL2 and the CorpVPN split-tunnel profile. I can ssh to bastion (by IP) but `curl http://config.internal/health` from WSL fails: "name or service not known". Outside WSL (PowerShell) I can ping the bastion by name. Anyone run into WSL DNS weirdness with split-tunnel?
IT Support Bot: (automated) Welcome Diego! If this is onboarding-related, please include your Windows public IP and we'll whitelist temporarily. Reply with `@IT Support Bot whitelist` to proceed.
Diego M.: thanks — my public IP is 34.91.12.77. I did `cat /etc/resolv.conf` in WSL and it shows my home ISP resolver, not the corporate DNS. I tried adding an /etc/hosts entry inside WSL but Docker Desktop overwrote resolv.conf on restart.
Nina (devex): WSL2 network is NATted and often gets Windows DNS behavior. Two paths we've used: 1) configure WSL to not auto-generate resolv.conf and set the corporate DNS manually, or 2) use an SSH tunnel via the bastion to reach services behind the VPC. Which do you prefer?
Diego M.: I don't want to modify global Windows settings if avoidable. Tunnel option sounds simpler. How do I get Docker to talk to registry.internal.redwood through the bastion?
Michael (infra-oncall): for Docker registry you can do an SSH local forward from Windows (cmd or PowerShell):
```
ssh -L 5000:registry.internal.redwood:5000 diego@bastion.redwood.internal -N
```
Then in Docker Desktop set the registry endpoint to `localhost:5000` or `docker login localhost:5000` from WSL. If you use WSL, run the SSH command from the Windows host (not inside WSL) so the port binds on localhost and WSL can access it via `localhost`.
Diego M.: ran the ssh forward from PowerShell, deploy-bot showed session open, can now `docker pull` in WSL. Thanks! What about hostname resolution for other internal services during dev though?
deploy-bot: (system) bastion session started for diego, audit id: a9b2c
Michael (infra-oncall): for persistent internal name resolution inside WSL, do this: in WSL edit `/etc/wsl.conf` and add:
```
[network]
generateResolvConf = false
```
then remove `/etc/resolv.conf` and create a new one with corporate DNS entries: `nameserver 10.12.2.2` and add search domain `search internal.redwood`. Finally run `wsl --shutdown` from PowerShell to restart the WSL daemon. That will make WSL use your custom resolv.conf.
Diego M.: ok that sounds doable but I need to be careful. Will this break my home browsing from Windows?
Nina (devex): no, it only affects the WSL environment. Windows itself keeps using whatever DNS your VPN/client pushes. If you prefer not to change WSL, we can fast-track a VPN config tweak to push the internal DNS suffix for split-tunnel clients — I'll create a ticket.
Diego M.: please do, that would help future hires. Also, do I need to remove anything later when I'm offboarded?
Michael (infra-oncall): if we push the DNS fix you won't need local changes. If you do the manual WSL change, keep the wsl.conf and resolv.conf as they are; on offboard we'll revoke your bastion key and firewall rules. I opened INF-4129 to add the DNS search to split-tunnel + a followup to document the WSL steps.
Diego M.: awesome, thanks y'all. For anyone else doing onboarding: if you hit WSL DNS issues, SSH local forward to the bastion is the quick unblock.
Nina (devex): welcome aboard Diego! ping if you want us to pair on the WSL edits so you don't accidentally change windows-wide settings. :wave:
